author: salivan
text:
Fxnewbie wrote: Here's my go at DBR and RBD. DBRs are numbered 1-3 and RBDs 4-6. Your comments are welcome. I have a question though. When you have price engulfing a DBR at 1a and later on goes to engulf an RBD at 5a, in which direction would you position a trade?

hiya Fxnewbie good question, the engulf of swing H/L is not important, it's right that our swing H/L represent supply and demand but we actually need to know what they self are reacted to, the DP that they reacted to in important for us to look for the ENG. any way always look more left and draw you boxes to more right of the chart and look for those DP that the supply and demand are reacted to, these can absorb a lot of FO. regards Salivan

author: salivan
text: hiya Pardis, it's not about open/close of candles it's about drawing you boxes from the worst dealers to where some exceeds others, assume you want to draw your supply zone (RBD) our upper band is where the worst buyers are and our lower band is depend on how much you want to make your zones wide and tight, but generally we extend it to where the sellers exceeds buyers.and very often this point will be align with the close and open of the candles. here is an pic from a master, hope it helps you
